AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.
  JUNE 20, 2024 AT 10:00 AM

  1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 10:00 AM
  Roll Call
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the June 20, 2024
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission was Posted on
  June 17, 2024 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

  2.  CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
   Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the May 16, 2024 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting

3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal

  Arts & Culture Administrator

4.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.

 6. ACTION ITEMS
  a. City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ – Design Concept Proposals for the
  Montrose Circular Benches
  1. Motion recommending that the City Council authorize the City Manager, or a designee,
  to enter into an Agreement for Commission of Artwork with an artist/artist team to design,
  fabricate, and install a public art piece for the Montrose Circular Benches in an amount
  not to exceed $300,000 dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund.
  b. Brand Library & Art Center and Glendale Unified School District’s Spring 2025
  Exhibition – Sponsorship Opportunity
  1. Motion approving (1) the funding of a proposal by the Brand Library & Art Center to

  1. Motion appointing two commissioners to the 2028 Olympics Committee.

9.  ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is July 18, 2024, at
  10:00 AM in City Council Chambers – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor Glendale, CA 91206.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting
  Approved as Corrected

  Thursday, June 20, 2024, at 10:00 a.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on June 20, 2024, at 10:07 a.m.
  •  Present: Commissioners Tufenkian Zadorian, Pogosian, Chairperson Vidor
  •  Absent: Vice Chair Yank, Student Commissioner Aleksandryan
  The Agenda for the June 20, 2024, Regular Meeting was posted on June 17, 2024, on the Bulletin
  Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the May 16, 2024 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting
  Approved as Amended

  •  Chairperson Vidor stated she wanted to elaborate on Item 7B of the May 16th Regular Meeting
  Minutes and stated that the Commission does have a standard operating procedure on handling of
  donated works and how they are reviewed and wants to look at expanding the existing procedure to
  include criteria for what the Commission and Staff approve of and don’t approve of.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Aleksandryan
  Abstain:  Commissioner Pogosian

3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal
  Arts & Culture Administrator

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts &
  Culture locations.

4. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS - None

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report. – No Speakers

  1
 6. ACTION ITEMS
  a. City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ – Design Concept Proposals for the
  Montrose Circular Benches
  1. Motion recommending that the City Council authorize the City Manager, or a designee,
  to enter into an Agreement for Commission of Artwork with an artist/artist team to design,
  fabricate, and install a public art piece for the Montrose Circular Benches in an amount,
  not to exceed $300,000 dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby recommends that the City Council authorize the City
  Manager, or a designee, to enter into an Agreement for Commission of Artwork with Kassia Rico to
  design, fabricate, and install a public art piece for the Montrose Circular Benches in an amount not to
  exceed $300,000 dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund, and Sage Vaughn as a second
  recommendation to go to Council as more fully outlined in the June 20, 2024 Report by the Library, Arts
  & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  •  Beau Basse of LeBasse Projects gave a brief recap of the RFQ process and stated four artists were
  selected as finalists, he also answered questions from the Commission. Artists gave a presentation
  of their proposals. The Commission asked questions and gave their recommendations.
  •  GiGi Garcia Vice President of the Montrose Shopping Park Association gave her input and asked
  questions.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Chairperson Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Aleksandryan
  Abstain:  Commissioner Pogosian

  b. Brand Library & Art Center and Glendale Unified School District’s Spring 2025
  Exhibition – Sponsorship Opportunity
  1. Motion approving (1) the funding of a proposal by the Brand Library & Art Center to
  provide programming support for the Glendale Unified School District’s Spring 2025
  Exhibition, and (2) the sponsorship in an amount not to exceed $8,000 from the 2024 -
  2025 Work Plan.

  •  Stephanie Sherwood, Exhibitions Coordinator for Brand Library and Art Center provided an
  overview of the sponsorship opportunity. The Commission provided their input and asked
  questions.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves (1) the funding of a proposal by the Brand
  Library & Art Center to provide programming support for the Glendale Unified School District’s Spring
  2025 Exhibition, and (2) the sponsorship in an amount not to exceed $8,000 from the 2024 - 2025 Work
  Plan, as more fully outlined in the June 20, 2024 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts &
  Culture Administrator.

  •  Commissioner Tufenkian had a clarification on Action Item 6b brought forth by Stephanie
  Sherwood and stated that the Commission does approve of the funding for proposal to support
  GUSD Spring 2025 exhibitions however, the funds should not be used for artists as a
  participation fee.

  2
   Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Aleksandryan
  Abstain:  Commissioner Pogosian

  c. Public Art Donation – “Ride like the Wind” by Catherine Hrenda
  1. Motion recommending that the City Council authorize the City Manager, or a designee,
  to enter into an Agreement for Public Art Donation with Catherine Hrenda for the artwork
  entitled, “Ride like the Wind.”

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby recommends that the City Council authorize the City
  Manager, or a designee, to enter into an Agreement for Public Art Donation with Catherine Hrenda for
  the artwork entitled, “Ride like the Wind”, as more fully outlined in the June 20, 2024 Report by the
  Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Aleksandryan
  Abstain:  Commissioner Pogosian

  d. 2028 Olympics Committee
  1. Motion appointing two commissioners to the 2028 Olympics Committee.

  The Commission hereby appoints two Commission Members to serve on the 2028 Olympics
  Committee, as more fully outlined in the June 20, 2024 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal
  Arts & Culture Administrator.:

  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a brief outline of what the Committee entails. The Commission asked
  questions and gave their input.

  Motion to appoint Chairperson Vidor and Commissioner Tufenkian to the 2028 Olympics Committee to
  serve a one-year term.

  Moved:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Aleksandryan
  Abstain:  Commissioner Pogosian

7. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2023-2024 Work Plan Progress

  3
 a. CITY WIDE ARTS
  i.  Mural Ordinance – No Update.

b. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS
  i.  Beyond the Box – Update:
  • Staff stated that the application for this year’s Beyond the Box program is currently open
  and closes on June 21, 2024.

c. PERFORMING ARTS – Update.
  i.  Brand Summer Music Series – Begins July 12, 2024
  • The Brand Summer Music Series will kick-off on Friday, July 12th at 7:00pm on the lawn
  area behind Brand Library. The series will take place on Fridays at 7:00pm through August
  30, 2024.

d. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No update.

e. MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS – No Update:

8. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  • Commissioner Tufenkian thanked Staff for all their work and stated she really liked all the projects
  that were presented today for the Montrose Circular benches, would love to see the finalists work in
  town in the future, and would like to keep the artists in mind for future projects and is happy about
  the selection today.
  • Commissioner Zadorian thanked Staff and wished everyone an amazing summer.
  • Chairperson Vidor thanked Staff and LeBasse Projects for the hard work done with Montrose art
  proposals and stated she was glad Montrose was enthusiastic about the artwork, she was happy
  about the choice that was made today on the artwork and agreed with Commissioner Tufenkian
  about working with the finalists on other projects. She also stated she went to Brand 52 Works on
  Paper art opening, and it was beautiful and encouraged everyone to attend. Chairperson Vidor
  asked if there was a way to follow the press coverage for Brand 52? Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated an
  Ace publicist hired Raw Studio to capture still photography and drone footage and stated Ace is the
  lead in reaching out to various press contacts in the city, they send a monthly report of the outreach
  they’ve done and its shared quarterly with the Commission. She also stated she can follow up with
  Ace about Brand 52 and share updates at the next meeting and have Ace present an update on all
  their outreach at an upcoming meeting.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones thanked Commissioner Tufenkian on all the hard work she did to narrow down
  the finalists for the Montrose proposals for the circular benches. The next opportunity for art review
  will be for the Fremont Park columns tile artwork and will keep the Commission updated as to when
  that will happen.

9. ADJOURNMENT : 12:23 p.m.

  Chairperson Vidor Moves to adjourn the June 20, 2024, regular meeting of the Glendale Arts and
  Culture Commission.

  Seconded : Commissioner Zadorian

The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is July 18, 2024, at
10:00 AM in City Council Chambers – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor Glendale, CA 91206.
